S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more major depressive episodes lasting at least two weeks, involving persistent low mood and/or markedly diminished interest or pleasure, accompanied by cognitive, somatic, and behavioral changes such as altered sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, and self-worth. Clinically, it requires significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning, and cannot be better explained by substances, medical conditions, normal bereavement, or bipolar-spectrum mood episodes. The course can be single-episode or recurrent, with episodes often triggered by psychosocial stressors but sometimes emerging without clear precipitants, especially in individuals with biological vulnerability. It is distinguished from adjustment disorders by severity and symptom constellation, and from bipolar disorder by the absence of manic or hypomanic episodes.

patient.personality: Bernice is a meticulous, nurturing organizer with a rich imaginative life who pours herself into creative arts and community storytelling.
patient.stressor: Bernice’s depressive episode began to take shape about a year after the death of her husband, when the flurry of immediate support from church and family had faded and she found herself alone in a quiet house most evenings. As the senior community organizer, she kept pushing herself to run quilting circles and storytelling events, but small mistakes in planning and the occasional missed detail started to weigh on her disproportionally, stirring up old memories of growing up poor and “being a burden.” Over several months she gradually withdrew from some of her beloved workshops and stopped initiating visits with the younger women she mentored, spending more time ruminating on whether she had done enough for her late husband and whether her life’s work truly mattered. She finally agreed to see a psychiatrist after a church friend noticed she had given away several cherished quilts, repeatedly described herself as “useless now that he’s gone,” and broke down in tears during a planning meeting, insisting every past misstep in her marriage and family was her fault.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t shake this feeling that I failed my husband and my family, like my whole life hasn’t amounted to much.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days now, from the moment I wake up until I go to bed, it feels like there’s a heavy gray blanket over everything, and even sitting in my own living room I just feel this deep, aching sadness and hollowness, like I’m already halfway gone myself.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to fuss over every detail of the quilting circles and love hearing the ladies’ stories, but lately I just stare at my sewing basket or let their calls go to voicemail because I can’t muster up any desire to plan, to sew, or even to sit and talk with them anymore.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: At night I lie there for hours with my mind running over every mistake I ever made with my husband and the children, and when I finally drift off I keep waking up in the dark, staring at his empty side of the bed and feeling more tired than when I first lay down.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep telling myself I was a terrible wife and mother, that I held my husband back and burdened my family, and I replay every little thing I ever said or did wrong until I’m sure they all would’ve been better off without me from the start.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: More and more, I find myself thinking it wouldn’t matter if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow, and on the worst days I catch myself picturing swallowing all my heart pills at once so I can stop being a burden to everyone, even though it scares me that I’m thinking that way.
